 Smith Village Hosts DMV, I-Cash Pop-Up Monday For Seniors 65 And Older
 Older residents age 65 or older can find out if the state owes them money or get DMV services Monday, Nov. 16, at Smith Village. 
 Lorraine Swanson , Patch Staff 
 Posted Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 12:18 pm CT CHICAGO—Older residents age 65 or older can find out if the state owes them money and renew or convert their drivers licenses into Real ID, and more on Monday, Nov. 16 at Smith Village , 2320 W. 113th Place, Chicago.
 Representatives from the Illinois Secretary of State DMV Mobile Unit and I-CASH will be onsite from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
 The Secretary of State's team can assist with renewing or correcting driver's licenses, converting existing standard driver’s licenses into REAL ID driver’s licenses, obtaining renewed or first time Illinois Standard or REAL IDs, issuing free state IDs for seniors aged 65-plus and purchasing license plate stickers.

In addition, Smith Village neighbors and residents are encouraged to stop in to talk with an Illinois State Treasurer’s representative to check the State’s records for more than $5 billion in unclaimed assets that it seeks to return to original owners or heirs at no cost with proper identification. No reservation is needed.
 However, advance registration for DMV Mobile Unit Services is required by calling the 19th Ward office at 773-238-8766 to schedule a 10-minute appointment between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. on Monday.
